messages:
Maya (Support): heads-up: Aurora-ML is seeing intermittent 429s in prod starting ~10:12 UTC. Customer reports ~8% failure rate on their ingestion API, all 429s. They say it happens every minute for a short burst.
Sandeep (Eng): can you paste the response headers from a failing request and a short sample of their client pattern? X-RateLimit headers or Retry-After would help.
Maya (Support): pasted from a failing request: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600/min`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000`, `Retry-After: 15`. Server logs show short bursts up to ~4.2k RPM lasting ~10-20s at the top of the minute.
Julian (Infra): that looks like minute-bucket rollover / boundary alignment. If a lot of clients start requests right after the minute resets you can spike above the per-minute quota briefly and hit Remaining=0. Are they doing many parallel short-lived requests?
Maya (Support): customer says they run 60 workers in parallel, tight 1s request loop, no jitter. They use streaming gRPC for ingest. Example pattern they shared: ```while (true) { client.send(payload); await resp; } // no jitter, no backoff```
Ryan (DevEx): streaming still counts as a request for RPM. If those streams are short-lived or they reconnect frequently, it multiplies. Two immediate mitigations: reduce concurrency or add randomized jitter between starts. Also recommend exponential backoff on 429 with jitter.
ops-bot: Deploy notice: ratecap-adjuster v2 applied 2026-02-10 02:00 UTC. No recent changes in rate-windowing.
Sandeep (Eng): double-check console for per-api-key quota: if they're on a plan limited to 3600/min that explains the header. Also verify they aren't sharing the key across multiple services/regions. We saw eu-west-1 ingress with the biggest spike.
Maya (Support): asked customer to capture request timestamps and token counts. They sent a trace (request_id=abc123) showing 74 requests started within a 6s window. They've applied a quick client-side cap to concurrency=20 and added 300-1500ms jitter.
Julian (Infra): short-term: we can enable a tiny grace burst if their use-case is spiky but short—manual quota bump for a few hours. Longer-term: recommend smoothing window on client (10s bucket) or client token-bucket. If they require sustained >3600 rpm, advise Dedicated capacity.
Sandeep (Eng): also check whether they are counting each streaming chunk as a separate RPC on their side. Our metrics count requests at start time; frequent reconnects look like new requests. Recommend keeping long-lived streams open where possible.
Maya (Support): customer implemented jitter+cap and added standard exponential backoff. After changes their 429 rate dropped to ~0.2% in our last 30m. They agreed to monitor 24h before requesting any quota changes.
Ryan (DevEx): I'll add a short note to SDK docs about minute-boundary spikes and provide a sample backoff snippet.
Maya (Support): closing loop for now; will re-open if 429s reoccur after 24h. :thumbsup:
